archetype.name: Pocket Passer (downfield)
archetype.definition: Love wins from the pocket by pushing the ball into the intermediate and deep middle of the field, and this year he has all but stopped running, so nearly all his value comes from throws of 10+ air yards.

report.headline: Volume is propping up a passer whose accuracy is only now coming back
report.take:
Jordan Love leads the league in passing yards and ranks second per game at 280.8, but that number mostly measures how often Green Bay asks him to throw, not how well he has thrown. The Packers' run game is the worst in the league by EPA, last of 32, and the offense passes more than the situation calls for (eighth in pass rate over expected). He is averaging 39 attempts a game, and the yardage follows. His efficiency is good, not great: 0.142 EPA per dropback ranks 17th, and his CPOE of -0.53 sits 26th, a fall of more than six points from last season.

Where he earns his value is clear. His throws of 10+ air yards added 56 EPA. Everything under 10 yards added 4.3, and the screen and behind-the-line game lost 11.4 on its own. Intermediate throws (0.606 EPA per attempt) and the middle of the field (0.561) are where he does his damage. Deep balls land only 32.1% of the time but still return 0.44 a throw. He is also far better under center (0.332 EPA, +9.7 CPOE) than in shotgun (0.084). This is a vertical passer who needs time and play-action looks, and he is being run through a quick-game offense that doesn't fit him. His time to throw is down 0.31 seconds from last year.

The accuracy drop is less alarming than it looks. Last year's +5.5 CPOE was a career high; in 2023 and 2024 he sat near +1. His 16.7% bad-throw rate matches his 2023 (16.9%) and 2024 (17.2%) levels, so 2025 was the outlier. The first three weeks did most of the damage: CPOE of -9.7, -13.6 and -8.5, including a Week 1 against Minnesota, now the top-ranked defense, where he was pressured on 47.8% of dropbacks. Over his last five games he is at +5.5 CPOE and 0.25 EPA per dropback, essentially his 2025 form.

Two weak spots are worth watching but not overreading. He has run only 11 times for 10 yards with one scramble all year, which removes a bailout he used to have (199 rush yards last season). His late-game work in close games is poor: -0.311 EPA, no TDs and 2 INTs, but that is only 36 plays. Neither cancels out what the last month shows, which is a quarterback back near his best with a pass-first workload that isn't going away.

strengths.title: Intermediate and middle-of-field throwing
strengths.body: His 10-19 yard throws return 0.606 EPA with a 59.3% success rate, and throws to the middle return 0.561 with +4.6 CPOE. That is where his arm talent and processing show up, and it held up across a shaky start. It has been the core of his game for three seasons, so it should last.

strengths.title: Locked-in passing volume
strengths.body: With the league's worst rushing EPA and an above-expected pass rate, Green Bay leans on him every week. His 280.8 yards a game ranks second, and he is on pace for 4,773. Nothing about the run game suggests that changes, so the floor on volume is high.

strengths.title: Accuracy has rebounded
strengths.body: Over the last five games his CPOE is +5.5 and his EPA per dropback is 0.25, both well above his season marks and right back to his 2025 level. The ugly opening weeks came with heavy pressure and a top defense. Since then he has looked like himself, and the career record says this is closer to his true level than the start was.

concerns.title: Short game is dead weight
concerns.body: Throws behind the line lost 11.4 EPA, and the whole under-10 group added only 4.3 despite a 69.8% completion rate. Some of that is scheme: a quick-game, screen-heavy approach is compensating for the worst run game in the league. Matthew Golden draws the most targets (83) at just 0.087 EPA each, which shows the volume going to low-value looks. It caps his efficiency more than it reflects a flaw in him.

concerns.title: Ball placement below his norm
concerns.body: A 16.7% bad-throw rate ranks 33rd of 38, and his season CPOE is down 6.1 points from last year. Some of that is a return to who he was in 2023 and 2024 rather than a new decline. Even so, he is a sub-average-accuracy passer on the season, and the 2025 version is not guaranteed.

concerns.title: Close-game and red-zone efficiency
concerns.body: In close fourth quarters he is at -0.311 EPA with no TDs and 2 INTs, and his red-zone EPA is negative even though 11 TDs came there. Both samples are small, 36 and 48 plays. The red-zone TD count is likely to cool more than the late-game issue is to persist.

trend.note: Three weeks of negative CPOE opened the year. Since Week 4 he has posted positive EPA every game, with peaks against Chicago and Carolina. The last three include a few more interceptions and a lower YPA, but EPA per dropback is still above his season mark.

nextGame.headline: New England's leaky deep coverage meets his best area
nextGame.body:
New England's pass defense is average overall (16th in pass EPA), but it bleeds downfield: 23rd in deep-pass EPA and 19th in explosive pass rate. It also allows 0.7 EPA a target to opposing WR1s, 31st in the league, which is exactly where Love's value lives. The counterweight is the pass rush, sixth in sack rate. His pressure-to-sack rate of 19.7% is solid, and he was hardly pressured against Carolina despite two line starters being out. The Patriots' offense ranks sixth in pass EPA, and Green Bay is a 3-point underdog, so expect a game script that keeps his attempts high. Against him at quarterback they allow 15.1 PPR points a game (10th-fewest), so the efficiency case is stronger than the fantasy-average case.

Availability is the swing factor. Christian Watson is questionable with fractured ribs but was described Monday as "doing great." He is Love's most efficient target at 0.463 EPA per target and the receiver who stretches this defense. Without him, more volume goes to Golden, the low-efficiency option. Left tackle Travis Glover, who played every snap of his four games, carries a return date of this game; guard Sean Rhyan is out until late November. On New England's side, A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson are out and Hunter Henry is questionable, which dents their offense and could take some shootout pressure off. Linebacker Gabe Jacas, questionable with a knee, would matter for the middle-of-field throws Love likes. Green Bay also comes in on ten days' rest.

keyMatchups.title: Vertical game vs. soft deep coverage
keyMatchups.body: Love's 10+ yard throws produce almost all his EPA, and New England ranks 23rd defending deep passes. If Watson plays, this is the most favorable shape the matchup can take. Kraft has the tougher draw, since the Patriots hold TE1s to -0.06 EPA a target.

keyMatchups.title: Patched line vs. top-six sack rate
keyMatchups.body: New England gets home at a top-six rate. Green Bay's line is missing Rhyan and possibly Glover. Love's quicker release this year and his Week 8 pressure rate of 2.4% suggest it can be managed, but one bad protection day like Week 1 swings everything.

nextGame.watch: Whether Watson suits up. Love's downfield edge against this secondary runs largely through him.

restOfSeason.body:
Volume is the most bankable part of his profile. A league-worst run game and a pass-leaning staff keep his attempts near 40, so 250-295 yards a game is a reasonable band even if efficiency settles. His accuracy should stay closer to the last five games than the first three, since the early slump came with pressure and a top defense, and his career CPOE says he is at least average. That points to EPA per dropback finishing better than his current 17th.

What likely regresses is the touchdown rate. He is on a 34-TD pace while his red-zone EPA is negative, so expect closer to 1.6-2.2 scores a game than a steady two-plus. Interceptions should hover around one every game or two, given his aggressive intermediate profile and an INT history in the double digits in 2023 and 2024. With almost no rushing, his fantasy value is purely passing, which narrows his ceiling against top QB scorers.
swingFactors: Christian Watson's rib injury and availability
Whether the run game improves enough to cut his attempts

confidence.note: Eight games with a clear rebound and stable volume, but injuries to his top target and two linemen add uncertainty.
